The L1 penalty it also declares is REFUSED with an error rather than ignored, and the iteration schedule it also declares is carried and not used because the direct solve returns the minimum an iterative scheme converges to

entries.reason: the fitted coefficients, the intercept first, and a prediction that is the intercept and the dot product of the features and the weights. A prediction of a different width is refused by name: a dot product of two vectors of different lengths is a truncation or an out-of-bounds read, and a caller who got a number back would believe a prediction about a model they do not hold
entries.effect: the prediction, or LinearModelError.shapeMismatch naming both widths
entries.source: the SDK 26.2 CreateMLComponents.swiftinterface; the refusals are this port's and the reasons are in the facts

entries.reason: the per-class coefficients in class-major order, an intercept per class and then one weight per class per feature, and the class distribution a prediction answers. featureCount is (coefficients.count - 1) / classes, because a two-class model over one feature has three coefficients and calling that two features refuses every prediction of it

the port's own error for the linear models: a width the model was not fitted for, too few rows, a design with no answer in some column, and an L1 fit that ran out of iterations. It is NOT Apple's surface - the SDK 26.2 CreateMLComponents declares no LinearModelError, its public errors are OptimizationError, EstimatorEncodingError, DatasetError and ModelUpdateError, and the surface has 0 rows for it - so it is recorded in the package's own registry, beside the code
entries.effect: the reason, in the framework's own words

entries.reason: FISTA - accelerated ISTA - for the L1 penalty: the exact prox of the penalty on the smooth part's gradient step, the step from the largest eigenvalue of X'X/n by power iteration on the device's own BLAS, the ISTA fallback at the ACCEPTED point when the extrapolated one overshoots (a shorter step from the extrapolated point tends to y, never to w, and the sequence cannot recover), and the KKT residual as the convergence test. Four defects, each producing a plausible wrong number, the last being the one that mattered: a rejected step's objective recorded as the reference (the run walked to 1e140); the fallback shortening from y instead of restarting at w; the convergence test on the objective's movement (it called a point 0.07 of objective above the minimum converged); and softThreshold's two branches the wrong way round, so every positive coordinate came out NEGATIVE - the sequence could not converge and the wrong test would not say so. With the sign fixed the residual at a penalty of 0.5 is 5.9e-9 and no single-weight nudge lowers the objective
entries.effect: the weights at the L1 minimum, the iterations taken, and whether it converged
entries.source: the algorithm is FISTA as published and the step from the device's own cblas_dgemv; the KKT condition and the single-weight nudge are checked by tests/backports/host/createml/l1, 9 checks, and the sign mutation is proven caught by that suite. Removing the ISTA fallback still passes it, which the facts record as the next strengthening
